title: The Detention of the band room
premise: Jude Thornbury has spent seven years hiding behind his anonymous coding handle, @thornbird, which exposes corruption no one should know about — including the school district's scheme to funnel band program funds into a board member's pockets. When his grandmother dies and leaves him a recipe box of coded instructions, Jude learns she ran the same kind of underground justice network he's accidentally become part of, and that her last unfinished 'recipe' targets the very people now threatening to shut down the band room where his found family rehearses. To expose the scheme, Jude must win the regional band championship that draws the auditor and press — while a rival student closes in on his identity and the district moves to erase the evidence. In the end, Jude chooses to unmask himself publicly, sacrificing his invisibility but saving the band, honoring his grandmother's legacy, and discovering that survival means nothing if you spend it alone.
about_author: B. M. Galloway is a former school music teacher turned novelist who writes about teenagers who refuse to wait for permission to do the right thing. They live in Ohio with a tuba they never learned to play and a filing cabinet full of other people's secrets.

chapters.title: Detention, Room 114
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Punished with a month of detention in the band room for a hack he didn't technically commit, Jude observes the ragtag detention crew: a drummer with anger issues, a clarinetist hiding bruises, and Ms. Okonkwo, the teacher who looks the other way. Beat: reluctant belonging begins.

chapters.title: Anonymous, But Not Invisible
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, alternating with his online handle @thornbird. He posts evidence of a city contract scam from the school library, heart pounding. A reply appears: 'You're getting closer than she ever did.' Beat: paranoia sharpened by curiosity.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: After Grandma Ruth's funeral, Jude inherits a wooden recipe box. Among the index cards are directions for 'Sour Grapes Casserole' and 'Burnt Offering Pie' — coded instructions, dates, names. The last card is unfinished. Beat: grief curdling into revelation.

chapters.title: Sectionals
chapters.summary: Priya's POV, the clarinetist. She reveals the district plans to cut the band program mid-year, funneling its budget elsewhere, and the detention crew vows to fight. Jude realizes his coding skills could help. Beat: the found family formalizes into a conspiracy.

chapters.title: Decoding Grandma
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Cross-referencing recipe cards with old newspaper archives, he confirms Ruth exposed fraud for decades — including a 1998 scandal involving the same school board member, Councilman Voss. Beat: awe and dread; the past is the present.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Ms. Okonkwo's POV. She announces the regional band championship — the one event that brings auditors, press, and the superintendent into the auditorium. If the band wins or makes noise, the cut becomes a public embarrassment. Beat: a fragile plan takes shape.

chapters.title: Practice Makes Enemies
chapters.summary: Deon's POV, the drummer. Rival band star and board member's nephew, Chase Voss, mocks the detention crew's ragtag ensemble. Deon nearly brawls; Jude talks him down. Beat: the enemy has a face, and it's smug.

chapters.title: Burnt Offering
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He executes one of Grandma's 'recipes' — a dead-drop of evidence to a retired journalist — and it works. But the journalist warns him: Voss has people watching for whoever continues Ruth's work. Beat: first taste of power, first taste of danger.

chapters.title: Priya's Secret
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Jude discovers she's been documenting her home situation and nearly deletes it to protect her; instead he helps her secure it safely. She figures out he's @thornbird and keeps his secret. Beat: trust deepens into something neither names.

chapters.title: The Audit
chapters.summary: Ms. Okonkwo's POV. A district 'audit' strips the band room of instruments and locks the storage closet. Ms. Okonkwo is threatened with termination if she interferes. Beat: the institutional squeeze tightens.

chapters.title: Sour Grapes
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Following a recipe card, he and Deon break into a district storage unit and find crates of 'disposed' instruments being resold privately — Voss's scheme in cardboard. They photograph everything. Beat: proof in hand, adrenaline high.

chapters.title: Chase Closes In
chapters.summary: Chase's POV, first time. He suspects Jude is behind an anonymous account that's been sniffing around his uncle's finances and starts laying a trap, planting a flash drive in the band room. Beat: the hunter becomes visible to the reader.

chapters.title: Intermission
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating short POVs during a stolen after-hours rehearsal. The crew plays badly, laughs hard, and Jude realizes this room is the first place he's ever been known. Beat: the emotional core — what they're actually fighting for.

chapters.title: The Trap Springs
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Chase plants evidence that Jude hacked the district servers; security drags Jude in. His careful anonymity shatters as his real name enters a disciplinary file. Beat: the price of the cause arrives due.

chapters.title: Grandma's Unfinished Card
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, in near-despair. He finally decodes the last recipe card: Ruth's final target was Voss, and the missing ingredient is a public forum — exactly what the championship provides. Beat: grief becomes inheritance; the plan completes itself.

chapters.title: Suspended
chapters.summary: Ms. Okonkwo's POV. Jude is suspended; the band is disqualified from regionals on a technicality. Ms. Okonkwo chooses to defy the district and file an appeal, risking her career. Beat: the adults finally stand up.

chapters.title: Reinstated, Barely
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The crew rallies — petitions, press calls to the journalist, community alumni testimony — and the band is reinstated with days to spare. Jude returns to a room that kept his seat empty on purpose. Beat: the found family holds.

chapters.title: Dress Rehearsal for a Heist
chapters.summary: Deon's POV. The crew plans the real performance: while the band plays, Jude will broadcast the storage unit evidence to every screen in the auditorium, with Chase's planted flash drive turned back against him. Beat: tension coiled, plan set.

chapters.title: Championship
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The band performs magnificently; mid-piece, the evidence floods the auditorium screens — Voss's scheme, the sold instruments, the audit trail. Chaos, then the press swarms. Chase's trap detonates on his own uncle. Beat: climax, triumphant and terrifying.

chapters.title: The Price
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Voss is investigated; the district retaliates against Jude anyway, and @thornbird's identity is now public. He loses his invisibility, his clean record, and nearly his college prospects. Beat: victory with a bill attached.

chapters.title: Encore
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The band room is saved, Ms. Okonkwo keeps her job, and the crew gathers in Room 114 — no longer detention, just theirs. Priya and Jude finally admit what they are to each other. Beat: warmth after the cost.

chapters.title: The Last Recipe
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, epilogue. He adds his own finished card to Grandma's box — 'Thornbird Pie: serves everyone the truth' — and passes a copy to a nervous freshman who knows too much. Beat: the legacy continues; justice outside the law becomes justice inside a family.
